sop_basis: TM22: "If the evidence shows the listed party is the counterparty or controls it, escalate"; resigned as director is not the same as no longer in control
rationale: The £2,400.00 payment PX-T596773223 to Stanford Consulting Ltd on 5 August 2026 matches invoice INV-7752, but list entry PX-L57053 (Robin Ferndale, born September 1970, under unresolved investigation, do not deal with companies he controls) matches the officer on name and birth month/year. REG-7106 shows he resigned as director only on 4 August 2026 and PSC-4454 shows he still held 60% of the shares until 7 August 2026, i.e. on the payment date. The listed party controlled the payee when paid, so the payment must go to the MLRO.

why_not.CLOSE: The matching invoice does not cure the fact that the listed person controlled the payee (60% PSC) on 5 August 2026.
why_not.RFI: Evidence already shows the listed party controlled the counterparty, so an RFI would risk tipping off rather than settle anything.

doubts: If the list entry's full DOB or address were shown to belong to a different Robin Ferndale, this would become a CLOSE; the match is on name plus month/year of birth only.

sop_basis: TM08 third-party funding; documented relationship explains a third-party payer
rationale: Bramgate Invoice Finance Ltd paid £89,895.79 (PX-T768398183) on 9 September 2026. Invoice finance agreement FAC-6518 (22 February 2026, predates the payment) provides 85% advances paid into this account, and remittance RMT-8608 dated 9 September 2026 shows 7 invoices totalling £105,759.75 x 85% = £89,895.79, matching to the penny. The third-party payer is a documented financier.

why_not.RFI: The agreement and remittance already explain the funding exactly; nothing is left to ask.
why_not.ESCALATE: No sign of crime: the payer, amount and date all match a pre-existing financing agreement.

doubts: If the remittance amount or payer differed from the credit, or the agreement post-dated it, it would need an RFI.

sop_basis: TM01 profile; "An account in the customer's own name elsewhere counts as their own account only when a document on file shows the customer holds it"
rationale: TM01 fired at 4.0x the monthly expected volume (£1,310,752.76 in 30 days), driven by £994,838.33 (PX-T850201706) on 11 September 2026 from account 51-91-47 10047996 in Wenley's name. The onward £964,993.18 to Oakdale Export Co matches pro forma INV-3056 and the customer's own sales order ORD-8811 (£1,343,031.75 from Stanbrook Hotels Ltd), but no document shows Wenley holds account 51-91-47 10047996 or that the £994,838.33 is the hotel's payment. Ask for a statement for account 51-91-47 10047996 showing it is held by Wenley and where the £994,838.33 came from.

why_not.CLOSE: The funding account is in the customer's name but no document on file shows the customer holds it, so the inflow is not yet evidenced.
why_not.ESCALATE: The spike is plausibly explained by a documented large order and a matching supplier pro forma; nothing indicates crime yet.

doubts: If the case reads the own-name account plus the PO as sufficient (4.0x is below the 5x own-account threshold), CLOSE would be correct.

sop_basis: TM01 profile; own-name account counts only "when a document on file shows the customer holds it"; below 5x own-account transfers close
rationale: TM01 fired at 3.3x (£1,416,458.33 received in 30 days), mostly £987,706.12 (PX-T483011855) on 5 October 2026 from account 34-82-15 19921012 in Ashwick's name, followed next day by £967,952.00 out to its own Spanish euro account (PX-T505615635). STM-2749 proves Ashwick holds the Lynworth Banco account (IBAN ending 5416) that received the outflow, but nothing on file shows it holds the UK source account 34-82-15 19921012. Ask for a statement showing Ashwick holds account 34-82-15 19921012 and the origin of the £987,706.12.

why_not.CLOSE: The document on file proves only the destination account, not the account that funded the spike.
why_not.ESCALATE: Money moves between accounts in the customer's own name, one proven; no suspicion arises.

doubts: If the case treats the round-trip to a proven own account as sufficient at 3.3x (below 5x), the answer is CLOSE OWN_ACCOUNT.

sop_basis: TM03 repeated payments £9,000-£9,999.99; "Payments of £10,000 or more need an invoice"; ESC_STRUCTURING: split to stay under a threshold
rationale: Four payments to Kingston Trading FZE (UAE) between 2 and 10 August 2026 of £9,680.10, £9,554.12, £9,805.29 and £9,552.56 total exactly £38,592.07, the INV-6362 total (payable in four instalments). However staff note NTE-7201 (2 August 2026) records the director asking whether splitting payments to Kingston below £10,000 would avoid the invoice requirement, showing intent to split to stay under the threshold. Each instalment was kept just below £10,000, consistent with that intent, so this goes to the MLRO.

why_not.CLOSE: The director's recorded question about splitting to avoid the invoice rule is a red flag the invoice does not neutralise.
why_not.RFI: Suspicion of deliberate structuring exists, so asking the customer would risk tipping off.

doubts: If the note were read as an innocent question and the instalment invoice as genuine, CLOSE INVOICE_MATCHES would follow since the sum matches to the penny.

sop_basis: TM08 third-party funding; TM04 >25 beneficiaries; "Once there is suspicion, escalate"
rationale: Whitford, a furniture importer, received £18,385.95 'COMMISSION POOL' from unrelated Ashley Promotions Ltd on 7 August 2026 (PX-T497732707) and within two days paid £17,850.44 (97%) as 30 'COMMISSION' payments to individuals in Italy, Portugal and Spain, including held payment PX-T452105741 (£442.09 to Noel Wencote). Payment file PAY-9751 matches the payouts but the 30 payees share just three addresses (10 each, with UK-style postcodes despite EU countries), and there is no agreement with Ashley Promotions or any commission business in the furniture-import profile. The account appears to pass a third party's money to linked payees.

why_not.CLOSE: No contract with Ashley Promotions exists and the payee file itself shows 30 payees on three shared addresses, so nothing explains the activity.
why_not.RFI: The shared addresses and an unrelated third party's money passed straight on are already suspicious; an RFI would risk tipping off.

doubts: A documented agency/commission agreement with Ashley Promotions and distinct payee addresses would point to RFI or CLOSE.

sop_basis: TM22: "A match on one detail alone does not prove it is the same party"; close only when evidence shows a different party
rationale: The £1,355.00 payment to Bromwick Print Studio Ltd (PX-T184420852) matched PX-L32516 only on the Kingsmere Works, Talworth address. why_not.ESCALATE: No link to the listed person beyond a shared building, and the payment is small and receipted.

doubts: If Parker Kingsmore appeared as an officer/PSC of Bromwick or the unit numbers matched, it would be ESCALATE or RFI.

sop_basis: TM01 profile; own-name account counts "only when a document on file shows the customer holds it"

sop_basis: TM01 profile; own-name account counts "only when a document on file shows the customer holds it"

doubts: A payment file matching all 33 payees would make this CLOSE; shared addresses or third-party funding would make it ESCALATE.

rationale: Hartford made four payments to Whitstead Arredamenti Srl (Italy) between 29 July and 7 August 2026 of £9,331.79, £9,238.46, £9,854.78 and £9,346.19 (total £37,771.22), refs 'WHITBROOK STAGE 1-4', each just under £10,000. sop_basis: TM03 repeated payments £9,000-£9,999.99; ESC_STRUCTURING "split to stay under a threshold"; once there is suspicion, escalate
rationale: Four payments to Milldale Trading FZE (UAE) between 1 and 9 August 2026 of £9,702.51, £9,763.87, £9,769.07 and £9,786.14 sum exactly to the £39,021.59 on INV-7480 (payable in four instalments). why_not.RFI: There is already suspicion of deliberate splitting; an RFI could tip off.

doubts: If the note were read as innocent, the penny-perfect instalment invoice would support CLOSE INVOICE_MATCHES.

sop_basis: "When transfers between the customer's own accounts explain activity at 5 times the declared income or volume or more, send an RFI for an updated expected income or volume"
rationale: TM01 fired at 7.3x (£8,431,280.00 received in 30 days to 15 October 2026), driven by £7,359,114.34 on 13 October 2026 (PX-T278615899) from an account in Glenholt's name, with £7,211,932.05 moved next day to its own Spanish account (PX-T537058784), which STM-722 shows Glenholt holds (IBAN ending 3637). why_not.ESCALATE: A financier paying an 'ADVANCE' to a trading company is a common, plausible relationship; nothing suspicious.

why_not.RFI: The invoice mismatch and unrelated high-risk goods already raise suspicion; an RFI could tip off.

doubts: Correctly dated, matching invoices for catering equipment would reduce this to RFI on the funding source.

Payment file PAY-3499 matches the payouts, but the 30 payees share just three addresses (10 each), and there is no agreement with Hollhurst Promotions Ltd nor any commission activity in the declared profile. The account appears to pass a third party's money on to linked payees.

why_not.CLOSE: No contract with Hollhurst Promotions Ltd exists and the payee file itself shows payees clustered on three shared addresses.
why_not.RFI: Shared addresses and an unrelated third party's money passed straight on already raise suspicion; an RFI risks tipping off.

doubts: A documented agency agreement with Hollhurst Promotions Ltd and distinct payee addresses would point to RFI or CLOSE.

sop_basis: TM08 third-party funding; GROUP_COMPANY "The counterparty is a verified company in the same group"
rationale: Everwick Group Holdings Ltd paid £69,365.90 'INTERCOMPANY FUNDING' into Lockby Fresh Produce Ltd's account on 16 September 2026 (PX-T846566682). Group structure chart GRP-9915 shows Everwick Group Holdings Ltd owns 100% of the customer and is itself 100% owned by Cameron Radford, who is the customer's director and PSC in register extract INC-176. Funding from the parent company fits the group, and the account otherwise shows routine own-account funding and supplier payments.

why_not.RFI: The payer is the documented 100% parent, owned by the customer's own director.
why_not.ESCALATE: Parent-company funding within a documented group is not suspicious.

doubts: There is no loan agreement for the funding, and the chart is the customer's own document rather than a registry extract for the parent.

sop_basis: TM06 higher-risk corridor (Lebanon); "A story that contradicts the records is a red flag"
rationale: Aldden Furniture Imports Ltd, a furniture importer that declared UK, Poland, Vietnam and China, paid £52,821.79 to Lynbrook General Trading SARL in Lebanon (higher-risk, undeclared) between 3 and 9 October 2026 (£18,231.27, £20,248.81 and held £14,341.71). Invoices INV-6812 match the amounts but are for "business consultancy and market access services", while the director told staff (NTE-8099) the payments were for furniture shipments from Turkey and could not justify routing funds to Lebanon. Records and story contradict each other, so the corridor activity is unexplained.

why_not.CLOSE: The invoices contradict the director's explanation and the Lebanon routing is unjustified.
why_not.RFI: Suspicion exists and the customer has already been asked; a further RFI risks tipping off.

doubts: A consistent goods invoice and a credible reason for the Lebanese account would point to RFI.

sop_basis: TM03 repeated sub-£10,000 payments; "An invoice, contract or payment file matches the amount, payee and date"
rationale: The four payments to Kelley Arredamenti Srl (12, 15, 18 and 21 August 2026: £9,469.59, £9,546.82, £9,490.51 and £9,214.78) match contract schedule CON-9471 (7 July 2026, Bramholt Brasserie fit-out fit-out) stage by stage to the penny and to the due dates. Buying Italian fittings fits the registered fit-out business, so the split reflects agreed contract stages.

why_not.RFI: The pre-existing stage schedule already explains every payment.
why_not.ESCALATE: Amounts and dates were fixed by a contract before the payments; no sign of deliberate splitting.

doubts: A schedule post-dating the payments or with different amounts would change this.

sop_basis: TM22; "A match on one detail alone does not prove it is the same party"; "If nothing on file settles it either way and nothing else is concerning, send an RFI"
rationale: Held payment PX-T482891403 (£920.00 'Garden landscaping' to Jesse Lynworth, UK account) matched internal list entry PX-L87926 (an individual exited in 2024 after unexplained third-party payments) on name only. Nothing on file gives the payee's date of birth or address to compare with the entry's (born 1996-05-23, 130 Wilton Gardens, Garfield), so the match is neither confirmed nor ruled out. The payment is small and the rest of the account looks like normal clothing-import trade. Ask the customer for the payee's invoice and details (full name, trading address) for the work.

why_not.CLOSE: Nothing on file shows the payee is a different person from the listed Jesse Lynworth, so the match cannot be closed.
why_not.ESCALATE: Only the name matches and nothing else is concerning, so the SOP calls for an RFI rather than escalation.

doubts: If the payee's details matched the list entry's date of birth or address, ESCALATE would follow; if they clearly differ, CLOSE.

sop_basis: TM01 profile; own-name account counts "only when a document on file shows the customer holds it"
rationale: TM01 fired at 4.0x (£3,125,292.89 received in the window), driven by £2,413,350.00 on 5 August 2026 (PX-T345226138) from account 23-34-43 22288315 in Dungate Apparel Ltd's name. why_not.ESCALATE: Funds arrive in the customer's own name with no other red flag; no suspicion yet.

doubts: A statement proving ownership would make it CLOSE below 5x (RFI_UPDATED_PROFILE at 5x+); proof the account is someone else's would make it ESCALATE.

sop_basis: TM04 more than 25 beneficiaries in 30 days; close only when "every alert explained by documents whose facts match"
rationale: Rayholt Software Ltd, a software studio declared as using freelance developers abroad, paid 36 beneficiaries (£354,665.11) in the 30-day window, including 33 'MONTHLY FEE' payments totalling £53,821.35 on 5-6 August 2026 to individuals in India, Spain, Poland, the US and Portugal (held/alerted payment PX-T158471359 among them). why_not.CLOSE: No document on file reconciles the individual payees, so the alert is not yet explained by records.
why_not.ESCALATE: Payments match the declared freelancer business model and are funded from the customer's own account; no red flags.

doubts: A payment file matching all payees would make this CLOSE; shared addresses or third-party funding would make it ESCALATE.

why_not.ESCALATE: A financier's advance to a trading company is plausible and nothing else is concerning.

doubts: A matching agreement and remittance would make it CLOSE THIRD_PARTY_DOCUMENTED.

doubts: If Jesse Thornwick were an officer/PSC of the payee or the unit matched, it would be ESCALATE or RFI.

doubts: A matching agreement and remittance would make it CLOSE THIRD_PARTY_DOCUMENTED.
